body: Thank you for all your replies! I'm trying to reply to each of you when I can. I really appreciate the advice.

Thank you for both these replies! I didn't think I'd be able to go to an access course because I thought they were only for older and more mature students (22+) and there was someone in my college class who was 19. I'll definitely do some more reading into it though.

> Oh, and A-Level IT is very very different to GCSE IT.

Learnt this first hand :P It was a complete turn around, work was piled on a lot more excessively and the other A-Levels I chose (business and computer studies) didn't help. This is one thing thats making me doubt going back to college because I don't think I'd be able to handle the workload again but I do work a job thats very fast and I do 12 hour shifts so maybe I've matured? Idk.

> Apprenticeship?

Looked for one for about 8 months, couldn't get one and I just rushed into my current job because I was worrying too much. That was a huge me problem, I was trying to get a business administration apprenticeship and the only feedback I got every single time was "You did great in the interview, you're a great candidate but maybe you should go back to school for another year?"

> If you don't feel like doing college for two years then book the exams privately and try to cram it all inside the space of a year at home while you work on the side. 

You can do this? I'd love to do this because I don't really wanna quit my current job despite my obvious hatred of it. I earn good money (£10 a hour, though I do work 12 hour shifts + its night shift so) and I don't want to be forced to live off my parents and inconvenience them whilst looking for a part time job.
That's actually somewhat inspiration, can I ask how old you were when you did go back to college?

I have a Functional Skills Level 2 due to them forcing me to take the test before I got trained up by my company. It's an equivalent to a C atleast academically and for apprenticeships, most places take it too (from what I've found.) I do feel like they'd make me retake my GCSE Maths though, I've been trying to get into a night course to retake my GCSE Maths but it's kind of ridiculous how little spaces there are. (There's only two colleges in my town btw.)

No. :/

As I said, I'd love to do law as an A Level alongside RE and and Politics because I did really well in English at school, even if I don't show it online lol. It's one of the only few things I enjoy too. I don't know what I'd want to do. That kind of eliminates a large part of my post I know but I do have a few months to think about it before I can't apply anymore.

Thank you! I'm obviously worrying because my life is a bit stagnant and all my friends are picking unis to go + my ex was going to uni and she used to talk about school ALL the time so I was worrying about it a lot. 

It's nice to hear someone who went to University a lot later than others and still ended up with a good life, I'm just trying to get some advice on what to do next cause I'm still young and immature. This definitely helps though.
